01.

Prospect Plus

Fall 2023 – Winter 2024
Logan Neighborhood, Philadelphia
Academic — Architecture / Urbanism · 20 weeks

A proposal to transform Philadelphia's Logan Neighborhood into a hub for arts and culture by repurposing an underused rail line that currently fragments the community. The project turns vacant, disconnected land into public and cultural space, aiming to give Logan a stronger identity within the city.

Program diagram
02.

Culinary Citadel

Winter 2023
Bartram's Garden, Philadelphia
Academic — Landscape / Architecture · 10 weeks

A culinary landscape that uses gastronomy and architecture to reshape food culture, bringing chefs from around the world to cook with what Bartram's Garden's farm produces. Visitors move through a multi-sensory, layered program built around seasonal, sustainable food.

Site axonometric
03.

Light Box Wellness

Spring 2022
Powelton Ave, Philadelphia
Academic — Architecture · 10 weeks

A wellness center defining health as healthy living rather than clinical treatment — removing the intimidation of hospitals in favor of a relaxed, community-facing space. Set in a food desert, it pairs an on-site food co-op with sloped-roof community gardens and zones for both activity and calm.

Site plan
04.

À Table: Epicurean Seater

Spring 2024
Academic — Furniture · 7 weeks

A chair born from the Epicurean idea of pleasure found in food and conversation, shaped by an imagined dinner-table gathering of Joan Didion, Susan Sontag, and Eve Babitz. Its strong lines echo the slicing of food, while its visible joints mimic a carefully plated dish — designed equally for a studio and a dinner party.

Section mock-up of the chair
05.

K-12 Design Education Research

May 2025
With the Lindy Center for Outreach · co-authored with Melanie Taylor
Research · 5 weeks

Documentation and reporting for Drexel's Lindy Scholars Program, supported by an Allstate Foundation College Service Grant, expanding youth-led design education through after-school workshops at five West Philadelphia middle schools. My role centered on analyzing and presenting two years of program data into a single coherent report.

Report cover
06.

Trashion Futures

Current — ending Spring 2026
Gikomba Market, Nairobi, Kenya
Thesis — Architectural Research / Urban Planning

A thesis examining Africa's clothing landscape through Gikomba, Nairobi — the world's largest second-hand clothing market, where imported Global North garments pile up with no disposal infrastructure. The project explores whether a space can be designed to plan for waste before it's created, reading the market's people, clothing, and structure as three interwoven layers.
